extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, students, and scholars interested in mathematical creativity and aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Poincaré's criteria for evaluating and producing mathematical work — aesthetic and procedural standards for what makes a mathematical result 'useful' or 'beautiful'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony of disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements are 'harmoniously disposed so that the mind without effort can embrace their totality while realizing the details.' Beauty consists in this unity-of-whole-and-parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results/formulations where the entire structure can be grasped at once yet the details remain intelligible; aesthetic unity is a primary selector of valuable combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy (minimal apparatus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A good mathematical entity uses minimal apparatus. Avoid superfluous symbols, hypotheses, or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element should be necessary; extraneous machinery or hypotheses reduce aesthetic and practical value. Economy functions as a test of necessity and elegance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Among equally valid combinations, the simpler combination is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple solutions exist, favor those with fewer assumptions, simpler constructions, or more direct arguments; simplicity is a tie-breaker for equally effective approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinations that surprise — that link previously unrelated domains — are the most valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value is placed on linking distant domains or producing unexpected connections; novelty that reveals new relations signals important mathematical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance (form of presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric elegance — the form of presentation matters as much as truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation and geometric or structural neatness are integral to judgement; an elegant exposition can increase the perceived value of a result even when the formal content is equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profundity
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth that hints at a wider law beyond the immediate result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results that seem to indicate a broader principle or generalization; the capacity to suggest a governing law or to open new vistas is a mark of depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (intelligibility without effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader's mind grasps the structure 'without effort.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of structure and argument is essential; if trained readers can apprehend the idea readily, the work meets an important aesthetic and communicative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry, regularity, and infinity as aesthetic signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Inner mathematical features such as symmetry, regularity, and relations to infinity signal beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for intrinsic structural features that historically correlate with mathematical beauty; these features often indicate deeper coherence and are aesthetically prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful = Useful (aesthetic merit as selector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poincaré's claim: 'The useful combinations are precisely the most beautiful.' Aesthetic merit is the working selector for mathematical truth, not a separate ornamental quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat aesthetic judgment as a heuristic for productive directions in research: combinations judged beautiful by trained taste are more likely to be fruitful or 'useful' mathematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic feeling as a cognitive faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of mathematical beauty functions as a cognitive faculty — a heuristic sense shared by real mathematicians that guides what is worth pursuing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize aesthetic reaction (the 'feeling of harmony') as legitimate guidance in choosing problems, methods, and formulations; cultivate the trained sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subliminal generation and selection (unconscious creativity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subliminal mind generates many combinations, but only those that are 'harmonious' rise to consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical creativity involves unconscious incubation; expect many candidate ideas to be produced subliminally, with the aesthetic sense filtering those that emerge into conscious thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages of mathematical work (production process model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-stage model: (1) conscious preparation (deliberate work on the problem), (2) unconscious incubation (setting the problem aside while the subconscious continues), (3) sudden illumination (solutions appear unexpectedly), (4) conscious verification (rigorous checking and write-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The creative process is iterative: deliberate practice prepares the subconscious; allow incubation and be open to sudden insights; follow with rigorous verification. Valuing these stages can inform how one organizes research and judges the provenance of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied judging questions for a result
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete evaluative questions implied by Poincaré: Does the result link distant domains? Does its form make the underlying law foreseeable even before all details are checked? Can the whole be grasped at once without losing the details? Is each element necessary (no superfluous machinery)? Does it produce the characteristic aesthetic emotion in trained readers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these targeted questions as a checklist when assessing a theorem, proof, construction, or formulation; they operationalize the preceding aesthetic criteria into assessment prompts.
